selector.champion: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma syndrome (MHIBCC)
selector.rationale: The presence of multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules, family history of similar lesions, and specific histopathological features support MHIBCC. The conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene further confirms this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Gorlin syndrome
rejected.why: The absence of characteristic features such as palmar or plantar pits and jaw cysts, along with a contradiction in the support notes, makes this diagnosis less likely.

registry.preferred_name: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma syndrome (MHIBCC)
support_spans: A woman in her 60s presented with multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored asymptomatic papules located on the face and vulva.
Family history was notable for a daughter with similar facial papules that had not undergone biopsy.
Eight lesions underwent biopsy, showing buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces.
Whole-exome sequencing revealed:    - A conserved splice-site mutation in SUFU gene (c.757-2A>G) in all tumor and normal tissue samples
